topic: Herdrm: A Native macOS Console for All Your Coding Agents
summary: herdrm (missuo/herdrm) is a native SwiftUI macOS console for the herdr agent runtime: one sidebar showing every space, coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Grok, OpenCode, pi...) and shell pane across your Mac and any SSH/Tailscale machine, with full-PTY attach instead of a chat wrapper. It is a client, not an agent and not a runtime - if the app dies, agents keep running. Verified 2026-09-28: 721 stars, 60 forks, 10 open issues, created 2026-08-19, 37 releases in 36 days (v0.1.0 to v0.6.9), 13,130 cumulative release downloads, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 license (commercial use needs a separate license), macOS 14+ and Homebrew cask herdrm 0.6.9.

competitors.title: Herdrm: One Mac Console for Every Coding Agent (Zentor Blog, Aug 20 2026, updated Sep 24 2026)
key_points: Frames herdrm as 'a console, not an engine': herdr holds the PTYs, herdrm is a thin SwiftUI client over a Unix socket in NDJSON frames
Distinguishes failure modes: if herdr breaks the agents stop; if the console breaks you only lose the view - the app owns no state the runtime doesn't already own
Remote devices work by forwarding the remote herdr socket over ssh -L with per-device 1s-30s reconnect backoff; auth via OpenSSH config, Tailscale SSH, or Keychain-stored password

Selecting a row runs 'herdr agent attach' and lands you in the real PTY/TUI, avoiding the broken-rendering class of problems that chat-shaped agent GUIs create (progress bars, diff viewers, permission dialogs)
Flags the default that 'nobody should discover by accident': the New Agent picker enables each agent's bypass-permissions flag by default (e.g. Claude Code --dangerously-skip-permissions)
Status is inherited, not inferred - herdrm renders whatever herdr's PTY watcher decided, so an agent stuck in a way herdr doesn't recognize looks busy
Documents the licence gap as of Aug 2026: repo shipped no LICENSE file, GitHub API returned null, reuse rights undefined though source is public
Reports growth curve: 448 stars the morning after the 2026-08-19 launch with 29 commits, 8 releases in the first day, 99.8% Swift
Notes the client-layer pattern: Heeler (iOS) credited for domain model, waku for sidebar design; clients appear once a runtime is popular enough that the terminal is the bottleneck

competitors.title: Herdr Review: The Agent Multiplexer Your Terminal Needed (andrew.ooo, Jul 8 2026)
key_points: Herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer purpose-built for coding agents - persistent panes, agent state detection, and a socket API in one binary
State model: every pane knows whether its agent is working, blocked, done, or idle; agents can drive the multiplexer back through the socket API (read/send/wait/split)
Snapshot data point for growth: 13,900+ GitHub stars, 4,500 new in one week, top-5 trending, v0.4.0, AGPL-3.0, installable via brew or curl one-liner (vs 41,234 stars on 2026-09-28)
Architecture: background server owns persistent PTY sessions; session > workspace > tab > pane hierarchy with agent state rolled up to the sidebar
Positions against tmux: tmux persists terminals, herdr persists agent workspaces and understands their state

competitors.title: Herdr Review: Open-Source Agent Multiplexer for AI Coding (bitdoze.com, Jul 10 2026, updated Sep 2 2026)
key_points: Runs inside whatever terminal you already use (iTerm2, Kitty, Alacritty, WezTerm, Ghostty) rather than replacing it - contrast with the desktop-app clients built on top
Single Rust binary ~10-11 MB, no Electron, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud dependency; runs on a $5 VPS and is reachable from a phone over SSH

Enumerates the multi-agent pain points herdrm addresses visually: no visibility into which agent is blocked, GUI wrappers that are Mac-only/Electron/replace the terminal, remote access as an afterthought, agents that cannot orchestrate each other
Reports 105 days old, ~15,000 stars, #1 on GitHub Trending on 2026-06-30, built by a single full-time developer
Client-server model: background session server manages PTYs that survive laptop sleep, WiFi drops and SSH disconnects; thin client renders the TUI

competitors.title: Herdr's own comparison matrix (herdr.dev/compare, Sep 2026)
key_points: The vendor's own framing: 'Apps manage the herd. Herdr runs it.' - herdrm is explicitly one of the clients of a runtime, not a peer of tmux/cmux/Superset
Matrix columns: herdr vs tmux/zellij (multiplexer) vs cmux/Warp (terminal app) vs solo/conductor/emdash/superset (manager app)
Key differentiator row: work survives its own UI closing - yes for herdr (server owns the terminals), only while the app is open for desktop manager apps
Semantic agent state (blocked/working/done/idle) is listed as herdr-only; manager apps show workspace status, multiplexers show process status
Worktree/diff review flow is a 'pairs with it' category (Conductor/Emdash/Superset core), which is exactly where herdrm's open issue #74 'support for the worktrees' lands

competitors.title: Pane vs Herdr comparison (runpane.com, Sep 2026)
key_points: A direct rival framing for the same buyer: Pane gives a desktop workspace for worktrees, visual diffs and git review; Herdr/herdrm keeps work in a terminal UI with a background server and detach/reattach
Shows what a native desktop client must add to compete beyond agent visibility: created/cleaned worktrees, built-in visual diff viewer, commit/push/rebase/squash/merge inside the app
Licensing split in this niche: Pane AGPL-3.0 vs Herdr Apache-2.0 (and herdrm PolyForm Noncommercial)
Herdr Cloud with a waitlist is coming, which pressures local-console clients to justify themselves on privacy/self-hosting

competitors.title: Herdr: Terminal multiplexer sorts fleets of coding agents (heise online / iX, Sep 11 2026)
key_points: Mainstream tech-press validation: states working/blocked/done/idle/unknown, current stable 0.9, Apache 2.0, Rust; Omarchy Linux integrates it
Herdr does not provide a language model and does not replace Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode - same 'runtime, not agent' framing herdrm depends on
Business context: founder Can Celik announced YC fall-2026 acceptance in early August; YC lists Herdr as a one-person company in Ankara; YC standard deal $500k; no other individual round mentioned

angles: Console vs runtime: herdrm is a client of herdr, not an agent and not a runtime. Kill the app and your agents keep working because the daemon owns the PTYs - that single architectural fact explains the whole feature list and the failure modes

Real PTY, not a chat wrapper: selecting an agent runs 'herdr agent attach', so diffs, progress bars, interactive prompts and permission dialogs render correctly; chat-shaped GUIs silently break all of them

One sidebar, every machine: remote herdr sockets forwarded over ssh -L with 1s-30s reconnect backoff; auth via OpenSSH config/agent, Tailscale SSH 1.98.0+, or a macOS Keychain password (never a file on disk)

The bypass-permissions default: the New Agent picker turns on each CLI's skip-permissions flag by default, which is coherent for detached sessions nobody is watching - and a real risk on the Mac holding your keys, credentials and working tree

Status is inherited, not inferred: the sidebar is only as good as herdr's detection, and only six agents report through lifecycle hooks (Pi, OMP, Kimi Code, OpenCode, Kilo Code, MastraCode). Everything else - including Claude Code and Codex - is classified from a screen snapshot, so an unrecognized stall can look busy forever

The licence changed the story: in August reviewers flagged that herdrm shipped with no LICENSE file at all; as of 2026-09-28 it is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, which is free for personal/hobby use but requires a paid arrangement for commercial use - unlike herdr itself (Apache-2.0)

Velocity as a feature and a risk: 37 releases in 36 days and a 0.6.x cadence means fixes land fast (text selection, SSH-to-Windows sockets, hidden-terminal CPU burn all shipped), and also that the version you install is not the one you will run next week; the app must chase herdr's own 0.9.1 breaking changes

What it deliberately does not do: no worktrees, no visual diff review, no git operations, no built-in agent of its own - the gap Pane, Conductor, Emdash and Superset sell into, and the top open feature request (#74)
Mac-only by construction: 99.8% Swift/SwiftUI, macOS 14+; Linux and Windows cannot run the console, though they can host the agents a Mac watches

Supply-chain caution is part of the onboarding now: signed by MOE AI LLC and notarized, but impersonation downloads distributing Windows payloads under the herdrm name exist, and the README's first warning is to install only from the repo or the Homebrew cask

faq.q: Is herdrm free and open source?
faq.a: Free to install and use, but not open source in the OSI sense: the repository ships PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, which permits noncommercial use, modification and sharing and requires a separate license from the maintainer for commercial use. Contrast herdr itself, which is Apache-2.0.

faq.q: Do I need herdr installed before herdrm works?
faq.a: Yes. herdrm will start a local herdr server for you if one is not running, but remote machines need their own herdr instance reachable over SSH.

faq.q: Does herdrm run on Windows or Linux?
faq.a: No. It is a SwiftUI app requiring macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer. herdr runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, so those hosts can run the agents a Mac watches.

faq.q: Does herdrm replace Claude Code or Codex?
faq.a: No. It is a console for agents that are already running under herdr - it never supplies the model or the agent.
Whatever herdr is running: claude, codex, gemini, grok, opencode, pi and more. The New Agent picker only lists CLIs actually installed on the target device.

faq.q: What happens to my agents if herdrm crashes?
faq.a: Nothing - the herdr daemon owns the PTYs and keeps running. You lose the view, not the work, and reattaching restores it.

It is inherited from herdr, which uses lifecycle hooks for a handful of agents (Pi, OMP, Kimi Code, OpenCode, Kilo Code, MastraCode) and bottom-buffer screen manifests for the rest, including Claude Code and Codex. Misdetected stalls can appear as 'working'.
